subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

The party was great and we **thoroughly enjoyed.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"had a ball"** means to** thoroughly enjoy oneself.**
 
• In the context of the sentence, **"had a ball"** is the most suitable idiom to replace** "thoroughly enjoyed".**
 
• The other options do not fit meaningfully in the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The party was great and we** had a ball**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In the dark:** This idiom means to be uninformed or unaware about something. It does not fit in this context.
 
• **Beat around the bush:** This idiom means to avoid the main topic. It is not suitable in the given context.
 
• **Cut corners:** This idiom means to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often compromising quality. It is not relevant here.
